collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a child aged 4-12; in the story (name1) uses an ear trumpet)

collection.description: A child asks to try an elder's shell ear trumpet: let the child try it, or show how to talk into it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has an ear trumpet made from a big spiral shell with the tip ground off, polished smooth from years of use. When someone speaks into the wide end, (subject) can hear them very well. (friend) has been staring at it all morning. Finally (friend.he/she) asks, very politely, if (friend.he/she) can try it.

choices.label: Show (friend.him/her) How to Talk Into It

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) shows (friend) how to speak into the wide end, not too loud, not too fast. (friend) tries. "HELLO," (friend.he/she) says, much too loud. (subject) winces. "Softer." "Hello." "Better." Soon (friend) is telling (subject) a very long story about a frog directly into the trumpet. (subject) hears every word. (subject.He/she) didn't really need to hear quite that much about the frog. (subject.He/she) listens anyway.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) hands it over. (friend) holds it to (friend.his/her) ear and points it at a bush. (friend.His/her) eyes go enormous. "There's a BEETLE in there. I can hear it WALKING." (friend.He/she) points it at the sky, the sea, the cooking pot, (subject)'s stomach. (subject) laughs and takes it back eventually. "Now you know why I'm always smiling at bushes," (subject.he/she) says.
